chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said:

I asked him about a man who had a concubine, and his son mounted her and had intercourse with her. He said: There was once a man who had a concubine and a wife, and the wife ordered her son to mount his father's concubine and have intercourse with her. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about that, and he said: 'That is not prohibited for the father, except that it is not fitting for him to have intercourse with her until she is cleared of pregnancy by the son. If a child results between them, the child belongs to the father, provided they both had intercourse with her in one day and one month.'

key_terms.يَسْتَبْرِئَهَا لِلْوَلَدِ: She is cleared of pregnancy by the son

ai.seo_question: Who is the father of a child if both the father and son have intercourse with the same concubine?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *luhuq al-awlād* (attribution of paternity) in the context of a father and son sharing a concubine, a scenario reflecting the social structures of early Islamic society. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that if both engage in intercourse within the same day and month, the child is attributed to the father, provided the concubine undergoes *istibra'* (clearing of the womb) to distinguish the lineage. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on clear lineage verification and the specific conditions under which paternal rights are affirmed over secondary claimants.
